title: Publish Python SDK, not the core app
note: Per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md, this task is implemented and its tests are written in this change, but manifest commands are not executed and status is not set to pass here. The orchestrator commits, runs the Wave 4 phase of the Book 3 final phased gate, and finalizes this evidence.

priorRelatedWork.note: MBR-308 (commit c2f13175, landed immediately before this task) already made packages/python/src/membrane_client/client.py pass a golden-fixture compatibility suite shared with the Rust and TypeScript clients (tests/sdk/python_client_test.py's PythonClientGoldenFixtureTest) and documented docs/sdk/http-transport.md's tools/call stub limitation. This task does not modify client.py, __init__.py, or python_client_test.py: it builds the publishing/packaging layer on top of that already-verified client code, per this task's title and description ('Expose typed client and analysis helpers on PyPI after contracts stabilize' / 'Publish Python SDK, not the core app'), and per its allowlist, which does not include changing the client's own protocol-handling source.

implementation.distributionBoundary: Added schemas/sdk-python-package-boundary.v1.schema.json (a new JSON Schema, additionalProperties:false, corePublishing.publishesCoreApp and corePublishing.bundlesDaemonBinary both const:false) and its instance packages/python/package-boundary.v1.json, which declares the sdist/wheel contains exactly one importable package (membrane_client), zero runtime dependencies, and none of engine/, apps/, packaging/, release/, install/, npm/, or packages/typescript/ (the core app, its installers/releases, and the other language SDK). tests/sdk/python_package_boundary_test.py mechanically checks the instance against the schema's required/const fields (no jsonschema package is installed in this environment; this task does not add that dependency, so the check is a small hand-rolled structural validator instead), then cross-checks the declaration against the real pyproject.toml (packages.find where=['src'], zero project.dependencies, no forbidden path substring anywhere in the file's text) and the real filesystem (setuptools' find: package-discovery rule reimplemented directly against the tree since setuptools itself is not installed; no forbidden binary/installer/archive extension present).
implementation.packagingReadiness: packages/python/pyproject.toml: version 0.0.0 -> 0.1.0 (matches the 0.1 semver baseline docs/sdk/publishing.md already declares for the Rust crates and the TypeScript client's package.json version); added classifiers (Development Status :: 3 - Alpha, Typing :: Typed, License :: Other/Proprietary License -- not a fabricated OSI classifier, since the repository LICENSE is the custom Orthic Labs Source Use License v1.0, not an OSI-approved license); added readme='README.md' (new packages/python/README.md) and license={text=...} naming that real license by name; added src/membrane_client/py.typed (PEP 561) plus [tool.setuptools.package-data] membrane_client=['py.typed'] so the package's own 'typed client' description is mechanically true for downstream type checkers; added include-package-data=false so a future unrelated edit cannot silently pull stray files into the sdist via setuptools' default auto-discovery. readme/license paths were deliberately kept inside packages/python/ rather than pointed at the repository-root docs/sdk/python.md or LICENSE (which would need '../../'): no build backend is installed in this environment to prove an out-of-package-directory path resolves under setuptools' build_meta, so keeping both references inside the package directory keeps the declared metadata testable today instead of asserting untested behavior. This is recorded as a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight.
implementation.daemonCompatibility: Added tests/sdk/python_daemon_compatibility_test.py, which reads schemas/context-receipt.v1.schema.json's properties.schemaVersion.enum ([1, 2]) directly at test time -- the same 'checked against the shared schema, not review' pattern MBR-308 applied to the operation-envelope golden fixtures -- and asserts analyze_receipt() accepts every version currently declared supported (today: schemaVersion 2 = current daemon, schemaVersion 1 = previous supported daemon, per that schema's own description: 'the planner always populates the v2 observability fields'), preserves correct non-degraded semantics for the oldest supported version on its own, and fails closed with ProtocolError(code='protocol_version_unsupported') against a version one past the newest the schema lists (a hypothetical future/unsupported daemon). This is a direct, deterministic demonstration of this task's acceptance criterion: 'Python SDK passes compatibility tests against current and previous supported daemon.'
implementation.docs: docs/sdk/python.md rewritten to stop claiming 'source-ready only; no PyPI publication claim exists' as the whole story (still true that no publish happened) and instead describe packaging readiness plus a new 'Daemon compatibility' section pointing at the new test and explaining what it proves. New docs/sdk/python-publishing.md mirrors docs/sdk/publishing.md's structure (written for the Rust crates under MBR-908) for the Python package: what the distribution boundary means, what packaging readiness was added, what the release gate is, and the same explicit 'publishing to PyPI stays a separately authorized release action; this source change does not publish, does not run a build, and adds no automation that could publish unattended' statement the Rust doc makes, applied to Python. docs/sdk/README.md gets a new section pointing at both new Python-only test files and explaining why they have no Rust/TypeScript equivalent (packaging concerns specific to a standalone PyPI distribution).

knownGap.description: This task cannot run an actual `python3 -m build` / `pip install` / sdist-and-extract round trip (analogous to what engine/crates/membrane-provider-sdk/tests/downstream_fixture.rs does for the Rust crates) because neither setuptools nor the `build` frontend is installed in this environment, and installing either is a new dependency not named by this dispatch and would also require network access this task does not have authorization to use. The packaging-boundary test therefore proves correctness by statically re-deriving the exact discovery/inclusion rules pyproject.toml declares and checking them against the real filesystem, not by performing a real build.
knownGap.recommendation: At the Book 3 Wave 4 gate, on a machine with network access and the ability to install setuptools/build (or inside the eventual xtask/local release-script MBR-903's local orchestration owns), run `python3 -m build --sdist --wheel packages/python` and extract the result to prove the real sdist/wheel file list matches packages/python/package-boundary.v1.json's allowedTopLevelPackages/forbiddenFileExtensions exactly, the same way downstream_fixture.rs proves it for the Rust crates. Until then, this task's static proof is the best available evidence within its allowlist and hard rules, and is recorded as a known gap rather than presented as an equivalent real-build proof.
knownGap.toolsCallStub: As documented in docs/sdk/http-transport.md (MBR-308) and repeated here in docs/sdk/python-publishing.md's 'Known gap': the shared McpServer::dispatch's tools/call branch is currently a stub for every tool call over any transport. This task's daemon-compatibility test proves schema/fixture-level version compatibility only; it does not and cannot prove a live round trip against a running daemon, and does not claim to.
